prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render.
Asset type: finished watercolor game-level environment concept, one continuous scene.
Input 1 is the EXACT SPATIAL LAYOUT reference: render only the large gameplay map within it, NOT its title, legend, sidebar, text cards, numbers, dashed arrows, or white margins. Input 2 is the approved ART STYLE reference from the preceding level: match its handmade watercolor illustration, mineral pigment paper grain, moss, oxidized brass, soft pale background and clear fine ink outlines on playable foreground. Do NOT copy its outdoor lake composition or mechanisms.

Create level 05, an abandoned garden pump-house inspection shaft seen from a microscopic spirit's viewpoint. Straight-on ORTHOGRAPHIC side elevation, camera perpendicular to the back wall, 2D platforming space; no isometric view, no angled room camera, no dramatic perspective. One landscape image around 3:2 to 16:10, filling the canvas with the whole continuous playable room. The room feels tall and vertical inside the landscape composition.

ENVIRONMENT:
Old faded terracotta brick and pale warm plaster, weathered pump cylinders, broad oxidized copper and iron pipework receding into a quiet blue-gray background, rootlets, soft sage moss, leaking mineral stains, a shallow muted teal sump at the very bottom. It is an indoor pump-house connected to the garden, not a brightly sunlit outdoor courtyard, not a Gothic castle. Much of the center/left is open vertical air space and muted softly blurred background masonry. Suggest the immense scale of an ordinary pump and thick pipe joints relative to a very small light spirit. Integrate all mechanisms into worn pipe inspection brackets and cast iron fittings, not randomly placed free-standing props. Sparse foreground roots frame the extreme corners without covering any landing or mirror. Do not add conventional lamps, glowing bulbs, a second window beam or luminous machines.

STRICT GEOMETRY, relative to the actual room (not the infographic margins):
1. Bottom LEFT, a small circular drain-pipe entrance from level 04 leads onto a short flat stone lip. A fixed tilted mirror M0 is mounted naturally in an old pipe flange on this lip. Beyond this lip the bottom is open water, with NO stepping stones or continuous floor to the right.
2. A at lower RIGHT: a wide horizontal old glass inspection shelf, transparent pale aqua glass on a narrow rusted rim, its top at about 80% image height. Its left portion extends over the open shaft; its right portion meets a substantial masonry landing. A single rotatable mirror M1 and physical handle stand on this shelf, with visible mechanical rotation stops. Its incoming light passes up THROUGH the transparent glass underside. Leave a clear standing area beside the mirror. This is a high ledge relative to the entrance, not connected to it by walkable ground.
3. B at middle LEFT: a closed rusty pump inspection chamber embedded in masonry, about 22-39% room width and 33-53% height. Show its interior in architectural CUTAWAY so the viewer can see a small wheel and safe interior floor, but keep its collision shell clear: closed top, bottom, left, and a solid right wall with only one tiny horizontal slit near the lower right edge. There is NO human-sized doorway into this chamber. The slit aligns with a possible ray from M1 but this illustration shows that old route SWITCHED OFF: do not draw any beam entering B. B's wheel is mechanically linked with a matte dark cable/rod routed along the BACK wall to the folding steps, with sensible joints. It is a control for the deployed steps, not an extra light source.
4. Three separately readable narrow, flat, unobstructed folding inspection steps climb beside the RIGHT wall: lowest at x87-95%, y70%; middle at x80-88%, y61%; highest at x87-95%, y51%. Then the last short hop goes LEFT to platform C at x75-85%, y44%. Their supports are small brackets on the rear wall, not extra climbable ladders. Exactly THREE intermediate steps; show them deployed. No pots, weeds, levers or roots on their landing tops.
5. C is a solid metal/stone control ledge, distinct from these three steps. Its handwheel controls mirror M2 through a visible slender dark articulated shaft behind the beam. M2 itself is a SUSPENDED MIRROR centered approximately x61%, y48%, clearly to the LEFT and a little BELOW C, hanging over empty air. NO floor, pedestal, step, catch platform or foothold immediately under M2. The mirror head and its distant handwheel must read as two parts of one mechanism. The outgoing ray from M2 passes well ABOVE the ENTIRE C standing surface; C is NOT in the effective light.
6. D at UPPER RIGHT is a small old glazed maintenance mezzanine at x79-94%, its transparent glass floor at y24%. Give it a closed top, a glass LEFT wall rising to the top, and a root-curtained small exit on the far right. It is NOT connected to C by stairs. The light enters D through its glass FLOOR. M3 is mounted here with a separate nearby handwheel and safe standing space. A short empty gap then a small hatch beyond the roots leads right/up to the greenhouse of level 06; do not shine another sunbeam through this hatch.
7. At the extreme upper-right back wall expose only a curved SMALL SECTION of the enormous immobile light-eating creature's SIDE/BELLY, layered ivory-white scales embedded behind old masonry and roots, no face, no eye, no complete creature. All ordinary scales are pale white. One required target scale is charcoal gray, with only a small warm amber contact glow beginning at its center where the beam lands; it must still be distinguishable from the pale body.
8. Include ONE tiny wick-light spirit, about 4% of image height, standing on D next to the final handwheel. Huge cream flame-shaped head, tiny limbs, a few wispy rear-head embers, watercolor white and warm gold, simple black oval eyes. No other characters.

ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS UNBRANCHED LIGHT PATH, precise and extremely important:
Show the FINAL aligned state only. One narrow crack HIGH AT LEFT emits one defined warm golden ray nearly vertically DOWN to M0 near bottom left. M0 reflects that SAME ray diagonally UP-RIGHT to M1 on shelf A. M1 reflects it UP-LEFT to suspended M2. M2 reflects it UP-RIGHT into M3 on mezzanine D. M3 reflects it a short distance UP-RIGHT into the dark target scale. Every segment physically meets the mirror at its turning point. Use a warm ivory core and restrained golden halo, no overexposure. Keep light much brighter than matte brown cables. NO light splitting. NO ray into B. NO ghost rays, arrows, debug lines, alternate solution paths, supplemental shafts, or stray ray from the hatch. Source -> M0 -> M1 -> M2 -> M3 -> target, and nothing else.
Approximate mirror positions in the room: source (10%,8%); M0 (12%,93%); M1 (76%,73%); M2 (61%,48%); M3 (86%,17%); target (95%,10%). Landing geometry must respect these points.

ART DIRECTION:
Use the warm poetic handmade watercolor look of input 2, but with quiet indoor shadows. Back wall/remote giant pump silhouettes: moderately softened edges, reduced saturation and contrast, pale translucent pigment washes. Retain visible watercolor texture and architecture, do not wash the scene to white fog. Foreground playable platforms, glass rims, mirror faces, handles, ropes and chamber slit: crisp thin charcoal/sepia ink outlines plus very subtle warm-white edge accents. Clear silhouette separation and empty landing tops. Cool misty sage-blue surroundings support warm ochre edges and the single luminous light route. Painterly, artistic storybook atmosphere, beautiful and materially believable, not photorealistic, not a glossy 3D render.

No captions, numbers, labels, legend, schematic inset, comparison panels, title, HUD, watermark or borders. This is the actual artistic scene rendering, not another flowchart.
